name: Belgium

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 11883495 inhabitants, recorded as 11.883 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in Dutch and French, in the transversal venues pass. Seven units, five houses and two stages, against an opening estimate of 3.5 produced with no research. Belgium is the first country where the count doubles, and the reason is the test being applied strictly: what is counted is a place where puppetry is shown, not a company that receives money. Belgium has many subsidised puppetry companies and the denominator excludes them by name; it has more halls than the estimate imagined. Flanders gives two, both freestanding houses. FroeFroe plays at Namenstraat 7 in Antwerp, having taken its own artistic course inside the Koninklijk Jeugdtheater complex from the 1997-98 season and gained a multi-year structural subsidy under the arts decree. Beeldsmederij De Maan holds its own theatre at Minderbroedersgang 3 in Mechelen — a hall of 175 seats, a second of 124 and a café, in the restored Holy Spirit chapel and house — and is a vzw supported by the Flemish government, the city of Mechelen and the province of Antwerp. Two of the four structurally funded Flemish figure-theatre organisations are not counted and the reason is the same rule: Theater De Spiegel and Ultima Thule are companies, and Ultima Thule works in residence in other people's halls, De Spil's Komedie among them. The denominator excludes funded companies without a venue and it is doing exactly the work it was written for. Brussels gives three. The Centre de la Marionnette de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, with its Musée des Arts de la Marionnette, sits at rue Saint-Martin 47 in Tournai and carries the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, the Wallonie and the Ville de Tournai; it is the designated puppetry centre of the French Community, and it is the weakest of the seven because part of its programming happens in the Créa-Théâtre rather than in a hall of its own. The Théâtre Royal de Toone plays in the impasse Schuddeveld off the rue du Marché-aux-Herbes, is the only traditional Brussels puppet theatre still working, is inscribed on the Brussels inventory of intangible cultural heritage, and shows the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, the Région de Bruxelles-Capitale and the Ville de Bruxelles. The Théâtre Royal du Peruchet has played since 1929 and for more than fifty years in Ixelles, in an eighteenth-century farmhouse holding its theatre and a free puppet museum, with the support of the Communauté française stated on its own pages beside COCOF and the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. Liège gives the two stages, and they are the discovery of the pass. The Théâtre Royal Ancien Impérial at the Musée Tchantchès, rue Surlet 56, is the oldest puppet theatre in Liège; it is run by the asbl République Libre d'Outre-Meuse, whose vocation is the folklore of the quarter rather than puppetry alone, so the theatre is a stage inside it rather than a house. It holds two master puppeteers and a team of five manipulators and plays from October to the end of April, Sundays at 10h30 and Wednesdays at 14h30 — a fixed weekly rhythm, which is what a diffusion venue looks like. The Théâtre de marionnettes du Musée de la Vie wallonne, Cour des Mineurs, has carried the Liège tradition in the same room since 1931, has its own programming from September to April, and sits inside a museum run by the Province de Liège: a named permanent puppet stage inside a larger public organisation, which is the case the ruling of 2026-07-27 was written for. Seven is a floor. The Théâtre à Denis, given as a puppet museum and theatre in Liège, was not read and may well be an eighth; the Liège tradition alone is denser than any other single city in the record so far. The record is disputed on that, and on Tournai.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. One establishment retained, the value moving from 0.5 to 1: ARTS2 Mons, a higher arts school of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation. Criterion read at source: a master's in puppetry arts, a standalone 60-credit master's opened in September 2020, run jointly with the Academy of Fine Arts and the Puppet House in Tournai, with a teaching team of fifteen. Puppetry is the object of the award itself and the school reports to the higher education ministry of the French Community. Counted at the establishment carrying the award: the Tournai partnership does not make three schools. The previous 0.5 was the midpoint of an estimated range. Upper bound at 2: the check covered the Wallonia-Brussels Federation and did not cover Flemish arts higher education, where a course could exist under another name.

establishments.name: ARTS² — École supérieure des Arts de la Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
establishments.description: The higher arts school of the French Community of Belgium. Its puppetry master's, opened in September 2020, is run jointly with the Academy of Fine Arts and the Puppet House in Tournai, and is the only state-backed puppetry qualification in Belgium's French-speaking system.
